methodology: Actual SampleScene and production cars/CPUs/items. Human profiles decide every 0.18/0.22 seconds, slew the physical wheel at up to 360 degrees/second and pedal at 3/second, observe forward traffic, and use the fast road-speed planner with small steering noise. Course-following input agents also approximate novice, cautious, intermediate, expert and aggressive control using distinct speed, reaction intervals, steering noise and jump anticipation; they are not human usability subjects. Includes a 12-second stop, 5-second input disconnection and operator result action. Drivers use InputManager and production input gates; never force vehicle pose, velocity, laps or outcomes. An agent responds to the public pedal-release notice after 0.35 seconds with 0.3 seconds of neutral input. Novice/cautious agents respond to a visible jump notice after 0.35 seconds by targeting 24m/s; understanding that cue is an assumed response, not a human-study result. Preparation is bypassed. Random seeds do not guarantee deterministic physics. Official and physics clocks are recorded separately. FORWARD-ONLY: player pedal is clamped to [0,1], no direction toggle or manual reset input; production automatic recovery remains active. Wall-stress adds a 1.6-second full steering mistake on a safe straight. CPU input is unchanged.
